findings.finding: Cell 4 source was edited after it ran. The saved source reads getattr(model, 'hf_device_map', ...) but the saved traceback shows model.hf_device_map. The edited cell was never re-run, so its current source has no matching output.

Every code cell has execution_count null, so the file cannot prove execution order or that all outputs came from one kernel session. The outputs are mutually consistent (one ipykernel id in the traceback) but this is not proof.

Weights were not SHA-256 verified. The notebook checked the snapshot directory name and Hub-reported file sizes only. The Hub LFS SHA-256 for model.safetensors at this revision is now pinned in configs/artemis_cuda_runtime.json; the CUDA module verifies it before load.

Quantization was requested, not inspected. No cell checked that modules were Linear4bit with nf4 weights; 8.7 GiB peak is consistent with 4-bit text weights plus unquantized towers/embeddings but does not prove it. The CUDA module inspects loaded modules.
AttributeError on hf_device_map: with device_map={'': 0} Transformers 5.20.2 did not set hf_device_map on Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration. The module reads parameter devices instead.

The checkpoint is bfloat16; T4 (compute capability 7.5) has no bf16, so non-quantized layers ran in float16. Gemma models can overflow in fp16. The three short cases produced coherent text, but longer prompts are untested.
Decoding used skip_special_tokens=True and never recorded whether generation stopped on EOS or on max_new_tokens. The module records finish_reason from token ids.

The notebook's prompt sent raw evidence objects; the repository path projects evidence through inference_input (adds empty title and source fields). Prompts in a reproduction differ slightly from the audited run.

Upstream chat_template.jinja (sha256 0a2c8073...) differs from the MLX community conversion's template (2f1b4d75...). CUDA and MLX outputs come from different prompts as rendered, weights and kernels; they must not be pooled.
Three cases, synthetic evidence, greedy decoding. This shows the runtime can generate contract-valid JSON; it says nothing about legal accuracy.

token_generation_vs_json_validity.json_contract_valid: 3 of 3 cases by the notebook's own validator, which matches gemma4_runtime.parse_response
